notes.meaning: Kohath was the father of four main family lines: the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites. Moses and Aaron came from the Amramite line. Even though this family held high honor, Moses gave no special rank to his own sons, leaving them to serve alongside the rest of the Levites.

The Kohathite males aged one month and older totaled 8,600. Even newborn babies were enrolled because God claimed them early to be trained for holy service. Their family task was to care for the most holy items belonging to the sanctuary.

The Kohathite families were ordered to pitch their tents on the south side of the tabernacle. Camping right beside the holy tent allowed them to guard it and quickly handle their duties. This location placed their camp directly next to the tribe of Reuben.

Elizaphan son of Uzziel was appointed as leader over all the Kohathite clans. God established clear leadership for every branch of the Levites so that work would be done in order. Under his guidance, the families cared for their sacred assignments without confusion.

The Kohathites were given charge of the tabernacle's most sacred furnishings. These included the ark of the covenant, the table for holy bread, the lampstand, the altars, and the inner curtain dividing the holy rooms. They carried these holy objects on the march after the priests carefully covered them.

Eleazar, the son of Aaron the high priest, was placed as chief over all the leaders of the Levites. He directed everyone who had duties in the sanctuary. As the second priest, he stood ready to oversee tabernacle life and take the high priest's place if needed.

The descendants of Levi's son Merari formed two family groups, the Mahlites and the Mushites. Although they had fewer clans than Kohath, their work was equally essential to God's tent. Every family had a designated part to play in worship.
The Merarite males aged one month and older numbered 6,200. This made them the smallest branch of the tribe of Levi. God still gave them a heavy and important share of the work.

Zuriel son of Abihail was chosen to lead the Merarite clans. They were assigned to camp on the north side of the tabernacle. Stationed there, they formed a protective line between the sanctuary and the other camping tribes.

The Merarites were entrusted with the structural parts of the tabernacle, including its wooden frames, crossbars, pillars, and heavy metal bases. They also cared for the posts around the outer courtyard, along with all the tent pegs and ropes. Because these materials were so heavy, their duty required great physical labor whenever the camp packed up to travel.

Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons camped on the east side directly before the entrance of the tabernacle. This was the place of greatest honor, facing the sunrise. They performed the sanctuary duties for the benefit of all Israel, and any unauthorized person who came near was to be put to death.

Moses and Aaron counted all the Levite males one month old or more, reaching a total of 22,000. Even with infant boys included, Levi was by far the smallest tribe in Israel. This official number formed the exact total needed to substitute for Israel's firstborn sons.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars note that adding the three clan counts equals 22,300, and they suggest a scribe made a copyist error in verse 28 by writing the Hebrew letter for six instead of three.

notes.meaning: The Lord told Moses to count and list by name every firstborn male in Israel who was at least one month old. God had set apart every firstborn son when He spared Israel on the night of the first Passover. Listing each child showed God's personal claim on every single family.

The Lord ordered that the tribe of Levi be taken as His own in place of Israel's firstborn sons. The Levites' cattle were likewise taken instead of all the firstborn livestock of the other tribes. In this way, one entire tribe was dedicated to God's full-time service so that the other families could be released.

Moses obeyed the Lord and counted all the firstborn Israelite males aged one month and upward. The total count came out to 22,273 boys. This counted only those born since the exodus from Egypt, which is why the number was so close to the Levite total.

The Lord repeated His command to take the Levites and their livestock as His own special possession. This clear command legally completed the exchange of the Levites for the firstborn of the people. God's authority as Lord guaranteed that this substitution was final and accepted.

There were 22,273 firstborn sons in Israel, leaving 273 boys without a Levite to take their place. God required five silver shekels for each extra child as a redemption price, which meant paying a ransom to release them. This payment was measured by the exact standard weight kept in the sanctuary.

The redemption silver was to be given to Aaron and his sons. The money belonged to the priests because the Levites had been appointed to help them with tabernacle work. Since there was a shortage of Levite workers, the silver compensated the priesthood for the missing men.

Moses collected the redemption silver from the 273 firstborn who were not covered by the Levites. The total amount gathered was 1,365 shekels of silver. Every part of the collection followed God's exact numbers and weights.

Moses handed all the redemption silver over to Aaron and his sons just as the Lord had commanded. The money was used to support the worship of God at the tabernacle. Moses showed faithful obedience by handling the Lord's silver with exact honesty.
